entries.new: visa on arrival, 30 days for the 17 the official list names; embassy visa for the 11 it does not
entries.note: The only official page we can read publishes one list and one allowance — 'may be issued a 30 day visitor visa on arrival' — and says citizens of all other countries need a visa before arrival. Publishing 90 days visa-free contradicted our own cited source. The eleven nationalities the list does not name are settled on the side that cannot mislead: a traveller who arranges a visa they did not need loses a fee, one who flies expecting entry loses the trip.

entries.reason: The business e-visa was cited to the tourist notice, which states a 28-day stay — the tourist visa's, not this one's. It now cites the business notice, which is the authority's own page for this visa and does not print the stay length, so it carries the official-portal mark.

entries.note: The official page states the visa is issued for 30, 60 or 90 days depending on the itinerary; we published the shortest of the three as though it were the only one.

entries.field: National (type D) visa fee — long stay, student, digital nomad, work
entries.note: Orden AUC/891/2024 raised the national long-stay visa fee to 90 euros, equalising it with the EU uniform visa fee after the Visa Code increase of June 2024. Our figure was the previous order's.

entries.reason: The 6,300 NOK figure is stated in the immigration regulation itself — § 17-10 first paragraph (a), "kr 6 300 i saker om arbeid eller studier" — rather than only on UDI's front page.

entries.field: National (type D) visa fee — residency, D7, D8, student, work
entries.note: Portaria n.º 91/2025/1 raised the national visa fee to 110 euros in March 2025; its own preamble notes the 90-euro figure had stood since 2011. Ours was the 2011 figure.

entries.field: Hong Kong, Serbia, South Korea, Türkiye — visa-free rows
entries.new: visa-free, with the portal's silence stated in the note
entries.note: The Immigration Agency's e-visa portal publishes a visa-free list of 60 nationalities that names Macau but not Hong Kong, and none of Serbia, South Korea or Türkiye, each of which we record under a bilateral arrangement. The portal's other column does not render for any reader we have, so we cannot tell absence from omission — the rows stand and the reader is told what the official list says.

entries.field: US-visa holders from China, the Dominican Republic and India
entries.old: AVE electronic authorization, 90 days, for Chinese and Dominican holders of a US or Schengen visa
entries.new: Visa-free with a valid US visa, no AVE: Dominican and Indian citizens 90 days (tourism), Chinese citizens 30 days (tourism or business); India added; Schengen visas do not qualify
entries.note: Resolución 316/2025 (in force since July 2025) lets Chinese and Dominican citizens with a US visa in a similar category enter without a consular visa or an AVE, and Resolución 353/2025 (August 2025) does the same for Indian citizens. The Migraciones AVE page repeats both. Neither resolution mentions Schengen visas. We still published the older AVE route, which is no longer how these three nationalities enter.

entries.field: Chinese and Indian citizens: AVE eligibility
entries.old: AVE available to holders of a US or Schengen visa
entries.new: Not on the AVE list; a valid US visa gives visa-free entry instead (CN 30 days, IN 90 days)
entries.note: The AVE page says Chinese citizens no longer need an AVE if they hold a US visa or green card, and that Indian citizens travelling for tourism with a US visa enter without one. Neither country appears on the page's list of nationalities eligible for the AVE.

entries.field: AVE qualifying visa for Filipino, Indonesian and Vietnamese citizens
entries.note: The AVE page requires, 'de manera excluyente', a valid US visa in category B2, J, B1, O, P, E or H-1B. It does not mention Schengen visas. The same correction is made in the summary and in the AVE fee note.
The page gives a stay of three months from the first entry, 'permitiendo múltiples entradas y salidas'.

entries.reason: The cash limits were cited to ARCA's front page, which does not state them. ARCA's travellers' page on bringing money in and out states the USD 10,000 threshold and the USD 5,000 limit for under-16s.

entries.old: USD 10,000 or more declared on arrival and departure; USD 5,000 limit for travelers aged 16 and under
entries.new: USD 10,000 or more declared on arrival; USD 10,000 or more can leave only by bank transfer, not in cash; USD 5,000 limit for travelers under 16
entries.note: ARCA says larger sums require the OM 2249A declaration on entry and must leave by bank transfer. The lower limit is for 'menores de 16 años', meaning under 16, not 16 and under.

Home Affairs now prices the Tourist stream (apply outside Australia) "From AUD250.00", read on the subclass 600 page and repeated in the sidebar of the 601 and 651 pages. Lower charges for Pacific Island and Timor-Leste citizens apply from 1 July 2026.
The First Working Holiday visa stream now shows AUD840.00, read twice today; the second and third visas show AUD1,000.00.

entries.reason: The cited page is the consular portal's index and states no country's regime; the Foreign Ministry's own table of entry visas (Quadro Geral de Regime de Vistos, updated August 26, 2026), linked two levels below it, states the regime and permitted stay for every nationality.
The cited page does not state the eVisa's fee or validity; the official eVisa portal's tourist-visa page states both ($80.90; valid 5 or 10 years, multiple entries).
The cited page does not state a passport-validity rule; the official eVisa portal's FAQ does, in so many words.
The cited page is Receita Federal's front page and does not state the cash threshold; the Traveller's Guide page on cash at entry does.
The cited page is the Ministry of Health's front page; its vaccination-for-travellers page states that no proof of vaccination is required for entry and when yellow fever vaccination is recommended.

entries.field: Chinese and Indonesian citizens: entry regime
entries.note: The Foreign Ministry's visa table (updated August 26, 2026) marks both with code 2: visa exemption for up to 30 days. The FAQ's example of a nationality needing a consular visa no longer names Chinese citizens.

entries.field: Armenian, Belizean, Bosnian, Grenadian, Micronesian, Moldovan, Mongolian, Namibian, Kittitian, Saint Lucian and Vincentian citizens: entry regime
Albanian, Dominican (Dominica) and Georgian citizens: entry regime
entries.new: Visa-free, up to 90 days in any 180-day period

entries.old: 90 days, extendable once by the Federal Police to 180 days per 12 months
entries.note: The visa table marks these nationalities' exemption with an asterisk: 'Maximum stay of 90 days every 180 days'. Germany and Italy, marked the same way, already said so; the extendable-days figure is removed from France, the Netherlands, Switzerland and Ukraine.

entries.old: At least 6 months, required for eVisa applications
entries.new: At least one month after arrival (6 months still recommended)
entries.note: The eVisa portal: 'Your passport must be valid for at least one more month after your arrival in Brazil', with a caution to check the airline accepts it.
Receita Federal states 'montante superior a US$ 10.000,00 ou o equivalente em outra moeda' on both entry and exit, under Law 14.286 of 2021.

entries.old: Enter only with an organized, locally-vetted guide
entries.new: Avoid all favelas, including tours marketed to tourists
entries.note: The FCDO's safety page tells visitors to 'avoid all favelas, including favela tours marketed to tourists'. The level is unchanged.

entries.reason: Proof of funds: the Visit Canada landing page does not state it; IRCC's 'Who can apply' page lists 'have enough money for your stay' among the basic entry requirements and says the amount varies with the length and kind of stay.

entries.note: The Consular Department's visa-free FAQ lists the UK among the 50 countries whose ordinary passports enter visa-free for up to 30 days, in force until December 31, 2026; the FCDO's China entry page says the same. The summary and the visa-free FAQ now name the UK.
Canada is on the same 50-country list, in force until December 31, 2026. The summary and the visa-free FAQ now name Canada.

entries.field: Greece, Cyprus, Slovenia, Brunei — entry requirement
entries.note: All four are on the Ministry's 50-country unilateral list; we had them as needing a visa. Brunei's exemption has no end date, the other three run to December 31, 2026.
The date we published had passed; the Ministry's FAQ gives the Russian exemption a separate end date from the other 48 countries.

entries.old: announced for one year initially (from June 1, 2025)

entries.field: Albania, Antigua and Barbuda, Georgia, Maldives, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Suriname, Uzbekistan — entry requirement
entries.note: The Ministry's Mutual Visa Exemption List shows an agreement covering ordinary passports in force for each (Albania 2023, Antigua and Barbuda 2024, Georgia 2024, Maldives 2022, Samoa 2025, Solomon Islands 2024, Suriname 2014, Uzbekistan 2025). The list's own note says stays under these agreements are generally limited to 30 days.

entries.old: trial unilateral visa-free entry announced in 2025
entries.note: Azerbaijan is not on the unilateral list; the mutual list shows its ordinary-passport agreement in force from July 16, 2025. The 30-day stay is unchanged.

entries.field: 240-hour visa-free transit — eligibility stated on visa-required rows
entries.new: removed from rows whose nationality is not among the 57 eligible
entries.note: The immigration administration's transit page lists 57 eligible countries. A shared note on 103 visa-required rows (AF, DZ, AO, BD, BZ, BJ, BT, BO, BW, BF, BI, CV, KH, CM, CF, TD, CO, KM, CR, CI, CU, CD, DJ, DO, EC, EG, SV, GQ, ER, SZ, ET, GA, GM, GH, GT, GN, GW, GY, HT, HN, IR, IQ, IL, JM, JO, KE, KI, XK, LA, LB, LS, LR, LY, MG, MW, ML, MH, MR, FM, MD, MN, MA, MZ, MM, NA, NR, NP, NI, NE, KP, PW, PS, PA, PG, PY, CG, RW, KN, LC, VC, ST, SN, SL, SO, SS, LK, SD, SY, TJ, TZ, TL, TG, TT, TN, TM, TV, UG, VU, VA, VE, YE, ZM, ZW) offered the transit to nationalities that are not on it.

entries.old: listed for Türkiye; missing for UA, VN, CZ, KG, LT
entries.new: removed for Türkiye; added for UA, VN, CZ, KG, LT
entries.note: Türkiye is not among the 57; Kyrgyzstan and Vietnam were added on August 20, 2026 (NIA announcement 2026 No. 4), and Ukraine, Czechia and Lithuania were already on the list.

entries.reason: The unilateral visa-free rows cited the consular site's front page, which states none of them. They now cite the same site's visa-free FAQ, which names all 50 countries, the 30-day stay and each scheme's end date. Russia and Brazil moved here from www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/, and the rows that had leaned on the default source now carry it explicitly.

Rows visa-free under a mutual exemption agreement now cite the Ministry's Mutual Visa Exemption List, which names each agreement, the passports it covers and its date of entry into force. Armenia, San Marino and Mauritius keep the default source: the list does not state their longer stays.
The 240-hour transit cited the immigration administration's front page; its own policy page states the 57 eligible countries and the 10-day limit.
Customs' passenger clearance guide states the declaration thresholds (RMB 20,000 in cash, or foreign currency equivalent to US$5,000); the front page cited before does not.

The cited page now redirects to the ministry's list of visa types, which names no nationalities; the ministry's "¿Necesito una visa?" page publishes Lists A, B and C of exempt passports, in so many words.
The cited page does not state the Visitor visa fee; the ministry's cost table, filtered to Visitante – Turismo, does.
The cited page does not state the passport or onward-ticket rules; the FCDO's entry-requirements page does, in so many words.

entries.field: Twelve passports we sent to the Visitor visa
entries.note: The Cancillería's List A of passports exempt from a short-stay visa names Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bhutan, Indonesia, Morocco, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Oman, the Philippines and Serbia, and List B names Hong Kong SAR.

entries.new: eVisa — Visitor (V) visa, with a conditional exemption
entries.note: The Cancillería places Nicaragua on List C (conditional exemption), not List A; only natives of the Caribbean Coast autonomous regions holding a US or Schengen visa or residence permit are named as exempt.
The cost table lists Visitante – Turismo at USD 56 study plus USD 82 issuance (EUR 44 + EUR 63 in Europe and Cuba).

entries.new: Valid on entry; 6 months beyond departure recommended
entries.note: The FCDO states the passport must be valid on entry, and that Colombian immigration authorities recommend an expiry date at least 6 months after the date you plan to leave.

The eVisa portal read on 31 August listed 66 eligible countries; on 25 September it lists 68, and the two it added are Guyana and Kosovo. Only the eVisa is recorded for them: the portal does not say whether the visa on arrival extends to the same two.
The page states a USD 50 visa fee plus a USD 50 online lodgement fee; USD 100 is the fee for extending a stay, and had been recorded as the visa fee.

entries.field: Tourist visa validity, stay and entries
entries.new: multiple entry, valid 1 year, up to 3 months per entry
entries.note: Read on 31 August the page said single entry, valid 90 days; on 25 September it says multiple entries, valid for a period of 1 year, permitted stay each entry 3 months.

entries.field: AVE eligibility — 66 nationalities (AL, AO, AG, SA, BS, BH, BZ, BJ, BW, BN, BF, BI, BT, CV, KH, CM, CI, CU, ER, SZ, ET, GA, GM, GH, GN, GQ, GW, MH, SB, KE, KI, LA, LS, MG, MW, MV, MU, MD, MZ, MM, NA, NR, NP, NE, OM, PW, PG, CF, CG, CD, RW, WS, ST, SN, SC, SL, TW, TZ, TG, TO, TV, UG, VU, DJ, ZM, ZW)
entries.new: embassy visa, or the AVE electronic travel authorization for holders of a valid US visa (tourist-embassy, ave)
entries.note: The Migraciones AVE page lists 69 nationalities under "Habilitados para AVE". Three (Philippines, Indonesia, Vietnam) already carried the AVE option; the other 66 showed only a consular visa. The page makes the AVE available for tourism to ordinary-passport holders of a current US visa in category B2, J, B1, O, P (P1-P2-P3), E or H-1B, so these rows now offer it the way the existing AVE rows do.

entries.old: not listed (visitor's visa from a mission, or the eVisa pilot)
entries.new: ETA added: online at eta.dha.gov.za, outcome typically within 24 hours, stays of up to 90 days extendable by 90 through the platform, arrivals at OR Tambo, Cape Town, King Shaka and Lanseria airports only; fee not published
entries.note: President Ramaphosa officially launched the ETA on 12 August 2026. The Minister's address says it was piloted for travellers from China, India, Indonesia and Mexico during the G20 Presidency, has processed 216 204 applications, and will 'progressively become compulsory' for visa-required countries, with embassies told as countries are added. Visa-exempt travellers may use it voluntarily. No fee appears in any official source we could read, so none is published.

entries.field: China, India, Indonesia and Mexico: application routes
entries.old: visitor's visa from a South African mission (plus the eVisa for China and India)
entries.new: still visa-required; the ETA is now also open to these four nationalities, alongside the mission route
entries.note: Requirement unchanged: the sources say the ETA is not yet compulsory and the ETA portal's own FAQ still points unsuccessful applicants to missions and the eVisa. Which other visa-required nationalities have been added since the launch is not published, so no other row was changed.

entries.field: Visa-free stay for citizens of Poland, Lithuania and Latvia
entries.new: 90 days from the date of entry (90 days per calendar year cap unchanged)
entries.note: The Foreign Ministry's page on the European visa-free regime says the stay is 30 days from entry for the 38 listed states, but 'for citizens of Poland, Lithuania and Latvia (including holders of Latvia's non-citizen status), the permitted stay is extended to 90 days'; the regime runs until 31 December 2026. We had all three at 30. Checked while following up the MFA's switch to new Visa Regulations (Council of Ministers Resolution No. 464 of 14 September 2026, published on pravo.by 17 September, replacing Resolution No. 1065 of 2010): the new rules leave our type C and D figures as they were: C valid up to 90 days, D multiple-entry and usually one year, a decision in 3 to 5 working days or 2 when urgent, a 60-euro fee on the MFA fee page, and EUR 10,000 insurance on the airport page.
